reference: McLaren 720S coupe (2017-2023), engineering reference only; the game uses a fictional name

model.note: Japanese type-approval code ABA-P14S seen on Commons photo captions

productionYears.note: Revealed Geneva, 7 Mar 2017; deliveries from May 2017; replaced by the 750S in 2023

body.value: 2-door, 2-seat mid-engined coupe, dihedral doors, carbon Monocage II tub incl. roof

usVsEu.value: Same hardware. EU quotes 720 PS / 770 Nm; US quotes 710 hp (SAE) / 568 lb-ft. DIN kerb 1,419 kg (90% fuel) vs US curb 1,424 kg (100% fuel). Spec rpm for peak power printed as 7,500 rpm in the 2017 press kit and Spider table, 7,250 rpm on the 2021 coupe table and US data.
usVsEu.note: Use 7,500 rpm as the primary figure

code.note: Evolution of the 3.8 L M838T; 41% new parts; built by Ricardo at Shoreham-by-Sea

layout.value: 90-degree V8, twin-turbo, dry sump, mid-mounted longitudinally

crank.note: M838T is flat-plane (Edmunds/Wikipedia); McLaren says only 'stiffer, lighter crankshaft' for M840T; evenly alternating-bank firing order below confirms a flat-plane pattern

stroke.note: Stroke +3.6 mm vs M838T (press release); 93 x 73.5 x 8 = 3,994 cc checks

compressionRatio.note: Same figure as the M838T; one US listing gives 9.0:1 for the Spider. Low confidence.

fuelSystem.value: Port fuel injection, 16 injectors (two per cylinder)

maxPowerRpm.note: 2021 coupe brochure table and US data print 7,250 rpm

torqueAtPeakPowerDerived.note: 530 kW / (7,500 rpm x 2pi/60); at 7,250 rpm it would be 698 Nm

fullLoadTorqueCurve.note: No official or readable dyno chart was found. Shaped through the factory points 770 Nm @ 5,500 and 530 kW @ 7,500 (675 Nm), with boost onset near 2,000 rpm and a progressive mid-range (evo: 'real build-up of boost through the mid-range'; Fabspeed tune gains peak at 3,700 rpm, implying the stock calibration holds mid-range torque back). Power from this curve: 443 kW @ 5,500, 523 kW @ 7,000, 530 kW @ 7,500, 520 kW @ 8,200.

value.BoostAddict_Aug2017: 694/696/698 whp (Dynojet), ~560 lb-ft (759 Nm) wheel, power peak at 6,500 rpm

measuredWheelDyno.note: Wheel figures within 2-3% of the crank rating imply the real crank output is roughly 760-800 PS (720S widely reported as under-rated). Torque given in wheel lb-ft referenced to engine rpm. No curve image could be read.

redline.note: Press release: revs to 8,100 rpm in 1st and 2nd, 8,200 rpm in the higher gears. Wikipedia/EngineLabs '8,500 rpm' traces back to M838T (12C) material; do not use.

limiter.note: Limiter assumed equal to the published max revs; cut style (soft ignition cut) not documented

idleRpm.note: Not published; typical warm idle for McLaren V8; cold start flare ~1,200-1,500 rpm (E)

launchControlRpm.note: Not published. Range 3,000-4,000 rpm likely; verify against an onboard launch video

firingOrder.note: M-Engineering (McLaren ECU specialist) page 'McLaren Cylinder Layout & Firing Order'; same order quoted on an owner forum for the 12C. Alternates banks every firing, as a flat-plane V8 must.

cylinderNumbering.value: Cylinders 1-4 on bank 1, 5-8 on bank 2; bank 1 is the right-hand bank
cylinderNumbering.note: 1-4/5-8 split is implied by the firing order (it alternates 1-4 and 5-8 groups). 'Bank 1 = right' is from an owner forum post (search snippet only). Which end cylinder 1 sits at is not documented: assume cylinder 1 at the cabin (timing) end, numbering rearward [A].

perBankFiringPattern.value: Bank 1: 1-3-4-2; bank 2: 8-6-5-7 (each bank fires like an inline-4 every 180 deg; banks interleave at 90 deg)

firingFrequency.value: f = rpm x 4 / 60 Hz (engine order 4): 53 Hz at 800 rpm, 200 Hz at 3,000, 367 Hz at 5,500, 547 Hz at 8,200; each bank/turbo sees engine order 2

type.value: Twin-scroll, ultra-low-inertia, titanium-aluminide turbines rated to 160,000 rpm

maker.note: Wikipedia cites OEM-turbo resale listings; part-label identification, not a McLaren statement

wastegates.value: Electronically controlled wastegates plus an electronically controlled dump (blow-off) valve
wastegates.note: Recirculating vs atmospheric dump not documented

maxBoost.note: Wikipedia says 'over 1.3 bar', uncited. Treat as approximate; 1.3-1.5 bar plausible [E]

boostOnsetRpm.note: From torque shape and reviews; not published

fullBoostRpm.note: Torque peaks at 5,500 rpm; calibration ramps boost through the mid-range

twinScrollPairing.value: Probably cylinders 1+4 and 2+3 on bank 1, 5+8 and 6+7 on bank 2 (pulses 360 deg apart per scroll)
twinScrollPairing.note: Standard twin-scroll pairing for a 1-3-4-2 bank; not documented

type.value: 7-speed + reverse Seamless Shift Gearbox (SSG), dual-clutch, Graziano

gearRatios.note: US OEM data feed; 3rd shown as 1.90 on carspecs.us. Not found in a McLaren document.

finalDrive.note: 750S has a 15% shorter final drive than the 720S

speedAtLimiterByGear.note: From the ratios, 8,100/8,200 rpm limits and a 0.335 m rear rolling radius. Factory 341 km/h top speed sits at the end of 6th; 7th is an overdrive

shiftFeatures.value: Ignition-cut quicker shifts; auto or manual via paddles; Comfort/Sport/Track powertrain modes

shiftTime.note: Not published; typical DCT torque interruption

differential.value: Open rear differential with McLaren Brake Steer (brakes the inside rear wheel)
differential.note: evo: open diff, Brake Steer simulates a limited-slip effect

stabilityAids.value: ESC with Variable Drift Control (driver-selectable slip angle)

measured.note: Autocar: 'brimmed with fluids'; C/D test weight 3,158 lb

simMass.note: DIN kerb + 75 kg driver, as for the prototype

comHeight.note: Typical mid-engine carbon-tub supercar; not published

rearWheel.note: Lighter forged options save up to 12.5 kg unsprung [F, press]

oeTyre.note: DragTimes car on 'OEM Pirelli P Zero'

optionTyre.value: Pirelli P Zero Corsa (about 6% more mechanical grip than the 650S); C/D Lightning Lap car ran P Zero Corsa

trofeoR.value: P Zero Trofeo R option not confirmed for the 720S in any source read (standard on the 765LT)

factory200to0.note: 117 m is 6 m shorter than 650S (launch press); 2021 brochure prints 122 m

airbrake.value: Rear wing deploys 100% as an airbrake in under 0.5 s under high-speed braking, shifting aero balance about 20% rearward

simTorqueEstimate.note: Enough to lock both axles at ~1.3 g with 41/59 static split and ~0.42 m CoM; ~61% front bias

dragCoefficient.note: McLaren never quoted Cd; see CdA estimate

CdA.note: Fitted so rated power (92% driveline, Crr 0.012, 1,494 kg) tops out at 341 km/h in 7th (~6,150 rpm); 0.91 if top speed is reached in 6th at ~8,100 rpm. Equivalent Cd ~0.46 on 1.85 m2, high because the wing is partly deployed at speed; a stowed-wing Cd of 0.36-0.40 (CdA ~0.70) would leave top speed set by the 6th-gear limiter (~345 km/h).

downforceVs650S.value: About 50% more downforce than the 650S (some outlets 56%); downforce-to-drag ratio more than double the 650S

rearWing.value: Full-width hydraulically actuated wing, up to 30% more downforce than the 650S Coupe wing. Modes: Driver Downforce 70-80% deployment by speed; DRS 30% deployment on straights; High-Speed Braking 100% in <0.5 s

bodyAero.value: Double-skinned dihedral doors duct air to the side radiators, so no side intakes; headlight 'eye sockets' duct cooling air; cooling 15% better than 650S; rear 145 mm lower than 650S

downforceAreaEstimate.note: About 1,600 N (160 kg) total at 250 km/h, ~36% front; not published, tune in testing

suspension.value: Aluminium double wishbones front and rear; Proactive Chassis Control II: adaptive dampers hydraulically interlinked at each corner, no anti-roll bars; Comfort/Sport/Track

pccSensors.value: 12 extra sensors: an accelerometer per corner and two pressure sensors per damper; reacts in 2 ms; control based on optimal control theory; 16 kg lighter than 650S system

noseLift.value: Vehicle lift raises approach angle from 8.3 to 10.4 deg
noseLift.note: Lift height in mm not published

lockToLock.note: Brochure prints '12.46', read as 2.46; Autocar measured 2.5 turns

steeringRatio.note: 443 deg of wheel per side over ~30.6 deg mean road-wheel lock implied by the 12.4 m circle and 2,670 mm wheelbase

springsEstimate.note: Ride frequencies ~1.6 Hz front / 1.8 Hz rear on the 1,494 kg sim mass

rollStiffnessEstimate.note: Stand-in for the hydraulic roll coupling of PCC II (real car has no bars)

factory.note: Spider: 0-200 7.9 s, 0-300 22.4 s, 1/4 10.4 s. Coupe 0-300 km/h not in the 2021 table (motor1.de text gives 21.4 s, internally inconsistent)

MotorTrend_2018_coupe.note: MT 'First Test', early 2018; original not readable

CarAndDriver_2018_coupe.note: Other C/D sheet values (0-100 mph, 70-0, skidpad, idle/cruise dBA) not reachable

AMS_2018.note: auto motor und sport comparison with 911 GT2 RS, as transcribed on a forum

DragTimes_2017.note: Owner's stock car, OEM P Zero, Palm Beach International Raceway

exhaustLayout.value: Each bank's exhaust manifold feeds its own twin-scroll turbo; catalysts after the turbos; rear silencer; two large round tailpipes set high in the centre of the rear valance, either side of the McLaren-lettered mesh panel, above the diffuser and below the engine cover/wing
exhaustLayout.note: Tailpipe position seen in Commons photo; turbo-per-bank and cats from press text/aftermarket listings ('factory converters'). Exact silencer and pipe routing not documented.

valves.value: Optional Sports Exhaust with a unique tailpipe design and 'even louder and more emotive' sound; valve hardware not described for either system
valves.note: Engine sound changes by ADP mode; aftermarket valved systems (Capristo, Fi, Novitec) are common

intake.value: Cast-aluminium plenum on top of the engine under a mesh cover (Speedmark logo lit on unlock)

turboCharacter.value: Audible 'whoosh' and 'fizz' under load; electronically controlled wastegates and dump valve. Wastegate chatter/flutter not described by the sources read
turboCharacter.note: Flutter on lift-off: [A] to be judged from recordings

interiorLevels.note: Idle 55 / 70-mph 75 come from a FastestLaps listing seen only as a search snippet (probably the C/D coupe test); unverified

euStationaryNoise.note: Not found. UN R51 test speed would be 3,750 rpm (half of S = 7,500 rpm) [A: rule recalled, verify]. Expect roughly 95-100 dB(A) [E]

limiterBehaviour.value: Hard stop at 8,100 rpm in 1st-2nd and 8,200 rpm above (gear-dependent limits). Cut type and bounce not documented
limiterBehaviour.note: Model as ignition cut, ~100-150 rpm hysteresis [E]

overrunByMode.value: Not documented. Reviews describe a muted, functional note; assume light crackle on lift-off only in Sport/Track, little in Comfort; louder with Sports Exhaust

bodyStyle.value: Low mid-engined coupe with a teardrop glass canopy, dihedral doors, no side intakes, flying-buttress-free rear (glass 'canopy' blends into a low engine cover), full-width active wing forming the tail trailing edge

windscreenBaseFromNose.note: +/-0.03. Base sits about 0.35-0.45 m behind the front axle; read from near-profile photos with perspective error

beltlineHeight.note: Door top roughly two-thirds of overall height

noseShape.value: Low, pointed, shark-like; deep headlight 'eye sockets' that double as intakes; front splitter close to the ground

tailShape.value: High, short tail: full-width wing as trailing edge, slim LED light blades, open mesh upper rear panel, deep diffuser, two round tailpipes high in the centre

Drag coefficient, frontal area and absolute downforce never published; CdA and ClA are fitted estimates.
Shift times, launch-control rpm, idle rpm, boost onset/full-boost rpm and exact max boost not published.
Firing order from one specialist source; cylinder-1 location and bank sides partly from an owner forum.
Exhaust valve hardware (standard vs Sports Exhaust) and overrun calibration by mode undocumented.
